The error is in item 9. The numbers 202530–202599 have six digits, but the problem only includes integers up to 99999, so they don't exist. That adds an extra 70 to the count.

The rest of the counting checks out:

- **Leading digit 3–9:** 77,777 numbers, all before 2025.
- **Numbers starting with 2 that precede 2025:** 1 (the number "2"), 9 (21–29), 90 (210–299), 7 (203–209), 900 (2100–2999), 9,000 (21000–29999), 70 (2030–2099), 700 (20300–20999), 4 (2026–2029), 40 (20260–20299), 1 (20252), 7 (20253–20259). These sum to 10,829.

So 2025 has $77777 + 10829 = 88606$ numbers before it, giving $i = 88607$.

As a consistency check, the numbers starting with 2 in range total 11,111. Of these, 10,829 precede 2025, 1 is 2025 itself, and 281 follow it. The 281 are: 20 (1), 200–202 (3), 2000–2024 (25), and 20000–20251 excluding 20252 (251). That gives 10,829 + 1 + 281 = 11,111, as expected.
